THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Two-Ingredient Sugar-Free Hot Fudge

Reusable dessert component — warm syrup + sifted Dutch cocoa, whisked silky in 30 seconds. Sub-15 cal, works on Creami pints, brownies, cakes, yogurt bowls.

YIELD1 serving
TOTAL TIME30 sec active
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~15 cal | ~1g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Warm the syrup 10-15 seconds only. Overheated syrup sets too thick as it cools.

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 1 tbsp sugar-free maple syrup (Maple Grove Farms filmed)
  • 1 tbsp Dutch-process cocoa powder (sift, don't dump)

Packaged labels vary — verify current sugar free syrup + cocoa labels before publishing final allergen or diet tags. Not vegan verified — some cocoa brands process on shared equipment with dairy. Check the current label.

You want a hot-fudge finish without the sugar hit or the 20-minute reduction. Two ingredients, one whisk, sub-15 calories per single-pint batch. Introduced as the topping on the Peanut Butter Bar Cookie Creami (W6F3 / Ep. 18) — cross-link back for the full parent recipe. Reusable anywhere a cold or room-temp dessert needs a fudge drizzle: Creami pints, warm brownies, protein cakes, yogurt bowls.

Method

  1. 1.MEASURE SYRUP. 1 tbsp sugar-free maple syrup into a microwave-safe ramekin. Maple Grove Farms was filmed; any sugar-free syrup works.
  2. 2.WARM SYRUP. Microwave 10-15 seconds. Don't overheat — overheated syrup sets too thick as it cools.
  3. 3.SIFT COCOA. Sift 1 tbsp Dutch cocoa into the warm syrup. Sifting is NOT optional — unsifted = gritty, sifted = silky.
  4. 4.WHISK. Whisk until no dry cocoa remains and the sauce reads silky and glossy. Aim for warm chocolate-syrup consistency.
  5. 5.DRIZZLE + SERVE. Drizzle immediately over the target dessert. Thickens as it cools — becomes a fudge shell over cold scoops.

Keys to success

  • SIFT the cocoa. Sifting prevents dry pockets and gives the fudge a silky finish. Unsifted cocoa = gritty texture — the recipe fails.
  • Whisk until glossy — no visible dry pockets. If the sauce reads matte or thin, whisk another 10 seconds.

If something fails

Fudge is gritty: The cocoa wasn't sifted. Restart — warm syrup + SIFTED cocoa, whisked. No fix once lumps set.

Fudge sets too thick / hard to drizzle: Syrup was overheated. Restart with 10 seconds max. If already too thick, thin with 1/4 tsp warm water and re-whisk.

Fudge is too thin / runny: Syrup wasn't warm enough OR cocoa dose was light. Warm 5 more seconds and add 1/2 tsp more sifted cocoa.

Fudge reads matte, not glossy: Undermixed. Whisk another 10-15 seconds until the surface reflects light.

Storage and reheating

Store: Make fresh — the fudge thickens as it cools and doesn't hold well overnight.

Reheat: 5-10 seconds microwave if made ahead. Whisk again after re-warming to restore gloss.

Lasts: Best within 5 minutes of whisking. Re-warmable 5-10 seconds if made slightly ahead.

Flavor target

Warm chocolate-syrup consistency at whisk time; thickens to fudge-shell texture as it cools onto a cold dessert. Silky and glossy — SIFT the cocoa or it's gritty. Background maple note from the sugar-free syrup, not maple-forward. Dutch cocoa specifically for the deeper alkalized chocolate read.
